page: Microsoft Azure L16as_v4 is a Lasv4-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and includes 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for cached small-block reads and large-block writes, though uncached large-block read bandwidth is relatively weak, falling in the bottom 25 percent. Text processing and small-model LLM text generation are highly efficient, while large-model LLM prompt processing is poor, landing in the bottom 10 percent.

From a resource density perspective, the L16as_v4 offers a high ratio of local NVMe storage to compute cores, making it a qualitatively cost-effective option for workloads requiring large, fast local scratch space without the overhead of external storage attachments. However, the tradeoff lies in the uncached memory read bandwidth, which may limit performance for memory-bound applications that frequently access large, uncached datasets.

This server configuration is suitable for database operations, local data processing, software compilation, and web serving. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing cores, 128 GB of RAM, and 3.8 TB of fast local NVMe SSD storage supports workloads such as relational databases, NoSQL stores, and intermediate ETL processing stages.
